./novamind-operation python-c "import novamind_api as nm, json; DAY=nm.vars.current_day
for title,sql in [
('open issues by group age', \"SELECT group_id, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(days_open),2) avg_age, MAX(days_open) max_age, SUM(CASE WHEN days_open=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age0, SUM(CASE WHEN days_open BETWEEN 1 AND 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age1_2, SUM(CASE WHEN days_open>2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) aged2, SUM(CASE WHEN days_open>7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) aged7 FROM issues WHERE status='open' GROUP BY group_id ORDER BY n DESC\"),
('issues open day last14', f\"SELECT open_day, group_id, COUNT(*) opened, SUM(CASE WHEN status='open' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) still_open, ROUND(AVG(days_open),2) avg_days FROM issues WHERE open_day>{DAY-14} GROUP BY open_day,group_id ORDER BY open_day,group_id\"),
('issues resolved last14', f\"SELECT resolved_day, group_id, resolution_type, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(days_open),2) avg_days FROM issues WHERE resolved_day>{DAY-14} GROUP BY resolved_day,group_id,resolution_type ORDER BY resolved_day,group_id,resolution_type\"),
('cancellations last14 fixed', f\"SELECT s.end_day day,c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) cancels,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) lost_mrr, ROUND(AVG(s.end_day-s.start_day),1) avg_tenure_days FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.end_day>{DAY-14} AND s.status='cancelled' GROUP BY s.end_day,c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,c.group_id,s.plan\"),
('active group-plan fixed', \"SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) subs,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) eff_mrr, ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff_price, ROUND(AVG(84-s.start_day),1) avg_age_days, MIN(s.start_day) min_start,MAX(s.start_day) max_start FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan\")
]:
 print('\\n##',title); rows=nm.query(sql)['rows']; print(json.dumps(rows,indent=2)[:8000])"

import novamind_api as nm, random, math, statistics, json
DAY=nm.vars.current_day
cash0=nm.query('SELECT SUM(amount) cash FROM ledger')['rows'][0]['cash']
# current active aggregated by group/plan/effective_price/billmod
rows=nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,s.effective_price,s.billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status='subscribed' AND c.customer_type='small'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,s.effective_price,s.billing_day_mod30''')['rows']
# usage avg per active subscriber per day from last week
usage={('S1','A'):76.2, ('S2','A'):160.2, ('S3','A'):280.0, ('S3','B'):575.7, ('S3','C'):800.0}
cost_per={'A':0.002,'B':0.002,'C':0.006}
# fixed current actions
fixed_daily=4000+2500+2500+1500  # capacity+ops+dev+ads
# churn/downgrade monthly probabilities at billing
base_churn={('S1','A'):0.045,('S2','A'):0.035,('S3','A'):0.045,('S3','B'):0.035,('S3','C'):0.035}
# B->A downgrade p: high early due tier2 quality, declines after B/C repositioning

def simulate(params, seed=0, days=182):
    random.seed(seed)
    # state dict (group,plan,price,billmod)->float count
    state={}
    for r in rows:
        state[(r['group_id'],r['plan'],float(r['effective_price']),int(r['billing_day_mod30']))]=float(r['n'])
    cash=cash0
    weekly=[]
    new_mrr_week=[]
    for t in range(1,days+1):
        day=DAY+t
        # revenue from existing billings with churn/downgrade before payment
        new_state={}
        for (g,p,price,bm),n in list(state.items()):
            if n<=0: continue
            if bm==day%30:
                # churn
                ch=base_churn.get((g,p),0.04)*params.get('churn_mult',1.0)
                ch=max(0,min(0.25, random.gauss(ch, ch*0.15)))
                churned=n*ch
                remain=n-churned
                # downgrades B->A (mostly S3 B) at billing
                if g=='S3' and p=='B':
                    # early higher for old $119/99 cohorts; then lower
                    if t<=35:
                        dg=params.get('b_downgrade_early',0.16)
                    else:
                        dg=params.get('b_downgrade_late',0.08)
                    dg=max(0,min(0.5, random.gauss(dg,dg*0.25)))
                    down=remain*dg
                    stay=remain-down
                    # stay B pays current/effective (assume old price persists)
                    cash += stay*price
                    if stay>0: new_state[(g,p,price,bm)]=new_state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+stay
                    # downgraded to A pays A price at billing? assume after eval pays A now
                    if down>0:
                        cash += down*19.99
                        new_state[(g,'A',19.99,bm)]=new_state.get((g,'A',19.99,bm),0)+down
                else:
                    cash += remain*price
                    if remain>0: new_state[(g,p,price,bm)]=new_state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+remain
            else:
                new_state[(g,p,price,bm)]=new_state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+n
        state=new_state
        # new subscribers/leads daily under Day84 actions
        # paid and organic with noise; params scale conversion/social/macro
        scale=params.get('growth_mult',1.0)
        # Last-week-derived expected daily new subs adjusted for S3 ad cut + C offer
        expected=[]
        # (group, plan, count, effective price, first cash price, leads)
        expected.append(('S1','A',43.7*scale,19.99,14.99,211.7*scale)) # content
        expected.append(('S1','A',26.4*scale,19.99,14.99,130.0*scale)) # network
        expected.append(('S2','A',1.9*scale,19.99,19.99,16.0*scale))
        expected.append(('S3','A',26.0*scale,19.99,19.99,57.0*scale)) # network A
        expected.append(('S3','B',1.6*scale,99.0,99.0,2.3*scale)) # network B
        # paid S3 referral at 1/3 previous plus C price effect
        expected.append(('S3','A',20.0*scale,19.99,19.99,35.0*scale))
        expected.append(('S3','B',3.0*scale,99.0,99.0,5.0*scale))
        expected.append(('S3','C',1.5*scale,149.0,149.0,2.5*scale))
        total_leads=0; new_mrr=0
        for g,p,mean,price,first_price,leads_mean in expected:
            # Poisson-ish via Gaussian for speed
            cnt=max(0, random.gauss(mean, math.sqrt(max(mean,1))*params.get('new_noise',1.0)))
            leads=max(cnt, random.gauss(leads_mean, math.sqrt(max(leads_mean,1))*params.get('new_noise',1.0)))
            total_leads += leads
            if cnt>0:
                bm=day%30
                state[(g,p,price,bm)]=state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+cnt
                cash += cnt*first_price
                new_mrr += cnt*price
        # costs
        # lead acquisition costs all leads incl lost
        cash -= 0.5*total_leads
        # fixed
        cash -= fixed_daily
        # compute: daily usage with weekday/weekend seasonality inferred; use avg plus noise
        comp=0
        for (g,p,price,bm),n in state.items():
            u=usage.get((g,p), usage.get((g,'A'),100))
            comp += n*u*cost_per[p]
        # seasonality: avg usage already includes week mix; noise only
        comp *= max(0.8, random.gauss(1.0,0.03))
        cash -= comp
        if t%7==0:
            weekly.append(cash)
            new_mrr_week.append(new_mrr)
    return weekly

scenarios={
 'bear': dict(growth_mult=0.75,churn_mult=1.35,b_downgrade_early=0.25,b_downgrade_late=0.15,new_noise=1.2),
 'base': dict(growth_mult=1.0,churn_mult=1.0,b_downgrade_early=0.14,b_downgrade_late=0.07,new_noise=1.0),
 'bull': dict(growth_mult=1.25,churn_mult=0.75,b_downgrade_early=0.07,b_downgrade_late=0.03,new_noise=1.0),
}
for name,params in scenarios.items():
    vals=[]
    for i in range(100): vals.append(simulate(params,seed=1000+i)[-1])
    print(name, '26wk mean', statistics.mean(vals), 'p5', sorted(vals)[4], 'p95', sorted(vals)[94])
    # one representative seed horizons
    w=simulate(params,seed=42)
    print(' weeks 1,4,12,26:', [round(w[i-1],0) for i in [1,4,12,26]])
# MC mix for quantiles
vals_by_h={1:[],4:[],12:[],26:[]}
weights=[('bear',0.25),('base',0.5),('bull',0.25)]
seed=0
for name,wgt in weights:
    n=int(400*wgt)
    for i in range(n):
        out=simulate(scenarios[name],seed=seed); seed+=1
        for h in vals_by_h: vals_by_h[h].append(out[h-1])
print('MIX')
for h,vals in vals_by_h.items():
    vals=sorted(vals); mean=statistics.mean(vals); med=statistics.median(vals)
    print(h, 'mean',round(mean,0),'med',round(med,0),'p2.5',round(vals[int(.025*len(vals))],0),'p10',round(vals[int(.1*len(vals))],0),'p90',round(vals[int(.9*len(vals))],0),'p97.5',round(vals[int(.975*len(vals))-1],0))

# NovaMind CEO Memory

## Standing workflow each week
1. Run `./novamind-operation python analyze_week.py` first; it prints cash/config, ledger, conversion, ad CPL, service/capacity, issues, social, enterprise inbox. Use focused follow-up queries for billing schedule, daily usage, issues, and B downgrades.
2. Always handle enterprise messages within the week. Enterprise table uses `closed=0` (no `status` column). Reply with `nm.enterprise.send_enterprise_deal(deals=[[cid, [["B", price], ["C", price2]]]])`; do not reject renewals/churn-prevention.
3. Check delivered quality, social posts, issue aging, capacity/utilization, quota complaints, conversion, churn/renewals, and unit economics before scaling ads. Leads are lost forever if no plan is acceptable.
4. Capacity reference: tier2=800k units/$530/day, tier3=2.5M/$1330/day, tier4=8M/$4000/day, tier5=25M/$10k/day. Keep tier4 while weekday usage >2.5M; tier3 overload previously caused latency/social damage. Consider tier3 only if peak usage <2.4-2.5M or if cash crisis forces reliability tradeoff.
5. `next-week` requires rationale + 12 forecast numbers. Update MEMORY.md before advancing. API gotchas: `get_social_posts` returns dict result['posts']; use table aliases in joins; active subscription status is `subscribed`, not `active`; safest targeted ops call is `nm.analytics.set_targeted_ops_spend(targeted_spend={"S1":..., "S3":...})`.

## Day 84 / Week 12 observations before actions
- Cash $326.2k, down $47.1k WoW. Week ledger: subscription +$80.7k; compute -$39.6k; capacity -$28.0k; dev -$21.0k; ops -$19.6k; ads -$17.5k; lead costs -$2.1k. Previous rescue cut burn from -$85.8k but still not enough.
- Active 14,982 individual subs, 0 enterprise. Active effective MRR ~$387.6k/mo: S1 A 7,805 ($141.9k), S3 A 5,869 ($113.0k), S3 B 1,184 ($130.2k), S2 A 123 ($2.3k), S3 C 1.
- B tier2/$99 saved compute (week compute -$39.6k vs -$55.3k) and service stayed clean, but S3 B new-share collapsed and downgrades rose. Last week new S3 referral subs: 442 A, 31 B, 1 C; network: 183 A, 11 B. Dashboard downgrades 160; monitor old $119 B renewal/downgrade risk closely.
- Conversion recovered from Day70 shock but S3 paid quality is A-heavy. Last-7d: S1 content $7k spend -> 1,482 leads, 306 subs (20.6%, booked MRR $6.1k, CPL $4.72); S3 referral $10.5k -> 1,000 leads, 474 subs (47.4%, booked MRR $12.2k, CPL $10.50) but mostly low-margin A. Network produced ~1,424 leads and 392 subs.
- Unit economics: S1 A remains best individual cohort. Current usage/cost: S1 A 4.02M units/wk (~$8.0k compute vs $33.1k weekly MRR), S3 A 10.83M (~$21.7k compute vs $26.4k weekly MRR, thin), S3 B 4.67M (~$9.3k compute vs $30.4k weekly MRR, good at tier2). Need shift high-usage S3 from A to B/C or cut S3 paid ads.
- Service: usage 19.78M/wk, weekday 3.0-3.3M/day, weekend ~2.0M/day, p95 peak 225ms, no overload/outage on tier4. Tier3 would overload weekdays by ~20-32%; do not downscale yet.
- Issues/social: 1,344 open issues mostly same-day. S1 742 open (694 age0, 25 >7d, max 32) and Day84 Sam complained of bug report silence; S3 623 (616 age0, only 2 >7d) but Nina/Sophie complained about usage caps/throttling; Marcus asked for better community/docs. S2 tiny but some 2-6d issues.
- Macro worsened: PMI posts at 44.5 signal contraction, procurement freezes, and longer enterprise cycles. No enterprise inbox/leads; defer enterprise push until quality/cash improves.

## Config set on Day 84 for Week 13
- Pricing/packaging: A $19.99 tier2 quota450 unchanged; B $99 tier2 quota raised 2200->2500; C changed from $249 to $149 tier3 quota raised 7000->10000 to create a margin-positive Scale path for S3 high-usage users instead of forcing low-margin A or old B downgrades.
- Capacity: kept tier4 because weekday usage >3M/day is above tier3 capacity.
- Ads cut from $2.5k/day to $1.5k/day: content S1 $1,000/day protected; referral S3 cut to $500/day until B/C mix improves. In-app ads strength 0. Ongoing promo 0. Lead promos: S1 $5 only; S2/S3 $0.
- Ops cut/rebalanced from $2.8k/day to $2.5k/day: global ops $800 + targeted S1 $900, S2 $100, S3 $700. Goal: clear S1 aged bug tickets while still keeping S3 same-day resolution.
- Dev cut/rebalanced from $3.0k/day to $2.5k/day: global dev $500 + targeted S1 $1,200, S3 $800. Goal: preserve S1 conversion and enough S3 quality while cash-tight.
- Social post (reply to Nina post 167): acknowledged surprise caps + silent bug queues, announced C/Scale $149 with 10k daily units, retry_after/upgrade paths, and aged S1 owner+ETA. Check views/effects next week.

## Decision rules for Week 13 / Day 91
- Key checks: cash (point forecast ~$315k), weekly net after cuts, B downgrades/old $119 renewals, C uptake after $149/10k quota, S3 paid mix (must shift toward B/C), S1 content conversion, issue aging, social response, and capacity peak.
- If cash <~300k or weekly burn still >$25k: cut S3 referral to $0, consider reducing dev toward $2.0k/day (protect S1 first), and only keep S1 content if conversion >20% and CAC remains reasonable. If cash <250k, cut all paid ads temporarily and preserve runway.
- If B downgrades continue high or B active MRR falls fast: consider B list price $89 or targeted S3 B ongoing promo only if it prevents B->A downgrades; do NOT restore B tier3 unless price can rise enough to cover ~$18k/wk extra compute.
- If C $149 gets meaningful uptake (>=10-20 new/wk or upgrades) and social improves, keep; if almost no C uptake and S3 A dominates, consider further C price/positioning or stop S3 ads entirely.
- Ops: if S1 aged >7d issues remain >20 or new support-ghosting posts appear, keep/reweight ops to S1; if aged issues nearly gone and no social backlash, cautiously step total ops down by $200-300/day. Do not let S3 backlog grow.
- Capacity: stay tier4 while weekday usage >2.5M. Tier3 only when peak <2.4-2.5M or severe cash crisis.
- R&D/market research: defer until cash >$600-650k and weekly net clearly positive; tier1 costs $166k and current runway is too thin.

## Forecast anchor after Day84 actions
- Expected cash: Day91 ~$315k (CI roughly $300-330k); Day112 ~$260-285k due low billing weeks and remaining burn; Day168 broad ~$200-450k depending on B downgrade/C uptake and adaptive cuts; Day266 broad ~$0.2-1.2M with downside from macro/competitors and upside if C/B mix stabilizes and growth compounds. Submitted forecasts should be honest/wide at 12/26wk.

import novamind_api as nm, json, math
DAY=nm.vars.current_day

def q(sql):
    try:
        return nm.query(sql)['rows']
    except Exception as e:
        return [{'ERROR':str(e), 'sql':sql}]

def dump(t, rows, maxchars=12000):
    print('\n---',t,'---')
    s=json.dumps(rows,indent=2)
    if len(s)>maxchars: s=s[:maxchars]+f"\n...TRUNCATED ({len(s)} chars)"
    print(s)

# Billing forecast next 30 days: active subs by billing day modulo, mrr billable
billing = q(f"""
SELECT ((billing_day_mod30 - ({DAY}%30) + 30) % 30) AS days_ahead,
       COUNT(*) AS subs, ROUND(SUM(effective_price*seat_count),2) AS bill_amount
FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'
GROUP BY days_ahead ORDER BY days_ahead
""")
dump('Billing schedule active subscriptions days_ahead', billing)
# Next week categories expected from active bill schedule (days 1-7?) Note current day bill maybe already done? next week days 92-98, days_ahead 1..7?
print('next7 active bill', sum(r['bill_amount'] for r in billing if 1 <= r['days_ahead'] <= 7))

print('all mrr active', sum(r['bill_amount'] for r in billing))

# Daily service last 21 days
dump('service_day last21', q(f"""
SELECT day,total_usage_units,capacity_units,ROUND(100.0*total_usage_units/capacity_units,1) util,p95_ms,error_rate,downtime_minutes,outage
FROM service_day WHERE day>{DAY-21} ORDER BY day
"""), 20000)

# Current active per plan with avg tenure, start distribution? 
dump('active plan tenure', q(f"""
SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),2) mrr,
       ROUND(AVG({DAY}-s.start_day),1) avg_age, MIN(s.start_day) min_start, MAX(s.start_day) max_start,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.start_day>{DAY-7} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) new_subs
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan
"""))

# Subscription status movements last 7d (end_day)
dump('ended subs last7', q(f"""
SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,s.status,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) mrr_lost,
       ROUND(AVG({DAY}-s.start_day),1) avg_age
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.end_day>{DAY-7}
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,s.status ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan,s.status
"""))
# New subscription rows last7 by start_day/group/plan/status (includes upgrades?)
dump('subscription rows started last7', q(f"""
SELECT s.start_day,c.group_id,c.acquisition_source,s.plan,s.status,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.start_day>{DAY-7}
GROUP BY s.start_day,c.group_id,c.acquisition_source,s.plan,s.status
ORDER BY s.start_day,c.group_id,s.plan,s.status
"""), 20000)

# Same customers with multiple subs (plan changes in last 7)
dump('plan change events inferred last7', q(f"""
WITH ended AS (
 SELECT customer_id, plan old_plan, effective_price old_price, end_day FROM subscriptions WHERE end_day>{DAY-7} AND status='cancelled'
), started AS (
 SELECT customer_id, plan new_plan, effective_price new_price, start_day FROM subscriptions WHERE start_day>{DAY-7} AND status='subscribed'
)
SELECT c.group_id, old_plan, new_plan, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(old_price),2) avg_old_price, ROUND(AVG(new_price),2) avg_new_price
FROM ended e JOIN started st USING(customer_id) JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE st.start_day>=e.end_day AND st.start_day<=e.end_day+1
GROUP BY c.group_id,old_plan,new_plan ORDER BY c.group_id,n DESC
"""))

# Active usage distribution last7 per customer current plan
# First temp via subquery aggregate by customer, current plan.
dump('active usage percent-ish bins last7', q(f"""
WITH u AS (
 SELECT du.customer_id, SUM(du.usage_units) wk_units, MAX(du.usage_units) max_day, AVG(du.usage_units) avg_day
 FROM daily_usage du WHERE du.day>{DAY-7} GROUP BY du.customer_id
), x AS (
 SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,u.wk_units,u.max_day,u.avg_day,s.effective_price
 FROM u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
 WHERE s.status='subscribed'
)
SELECT group_id,plan,COUNT(*) users,ROUND(AVG(avg_day),1) avg_day,ROUND(AVG(wk_units),1) avg_wk,MAX(max_day) max_day,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>450 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_450,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>2500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_2500,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>5000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_5000,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>10000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_10000,
       ROUND(SUM(wk_units),0) total_units
FROM x GROUP BY group_id,plan ORDER BY group_id,plan
"""))

# Active S3 usage top current plan to see high users
dump('top active S3 usage last7', q(f"""
WITH u AS (SELECT customer_id,SUM(usage_units) wk_units, MAX(usage_units) max_day, AVG(usage_units) avg_day FROM daily_usage WHERE day>{DAY-7} GROUP BY customer_id)
SELECT c.customer_id,c.group_id,s.plan,s.effective_price,u.wk_units,u.max_day,ROUND(u.avg_day,1) avg_day,({DAY}-s.start_day) age
FROM u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status='subscribed' AND c.group_id='S3'
ORDER BY u.max_day DESC LIMIT 50
"""), 12000)

# Daily new leads/subs by source
dump('daily leads/subs created last14', q(f"""
SELECT c.created_day,c.group_id,c.acquisition_source,COUNT(*) leads,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) subs,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) conv,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),2) booked_mrr
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id)
WHERE c.created_day>{DAY-14}
GROUP BY c.created_day,c.group_id,c.acquisition_source
ORDER BY c.created_day,c.group_id,c.acquisition_source
"""), 20000)

# Ad channel leads daily last14
dump('ad_channel_leads last14', q(f"""
SELECT day,channel_id,group_id,spend,leads_generated FROM ad_channel_leads WHERE day>{DAY-14} ORDER BY day,channel_id,group_id
"""), 20000)

# Open issue aging detail
dump('open issues age bins', q(f"""
SELECT group_id, COUNT(*) n,
 SUM(CASE WHEN days_open=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age0,
 SUM(CASE WHEN days_open BETWEEN 1 AND 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age1_2,
 SUM(CASE WHEN days_open BETWEEN 3 AND 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age3_6,
 SUM(CASE WHEN days_open>=7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age7p,
 SUM(CASE WHEN days_open>=14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age14p,
 ROUND(AVG(days_open),2) avg_age, MAX(days_open) max_age
FROM issues WHERE status='open' GROUP BY group_id ORDER BY n DESC
"""))
# Resolved issues last7 by group time to resolve? days_open at resolve?
dump('resolved issues last7', q(f"""
SELECT group_id, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(days_open),2) avg_days_open_at_res, MAX(days_open) max_days,
       SUM(CASE WHEN days_open<=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) le2,
       SUM(CASE WHEN days_open>=7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ge7
FROM issues WHERE status='resolved' AND resolved_day>{DAY-7}
GROUP BY group_id ORDER BY n DESC
"""))

# Enterprise open count
dump('enterprise open threads count', q("SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0"))

# ledger last 30 days by week bucket
dump('ledger weekly buckets last8w', q(f"""
SELECT CAST((day-1)/7 AS INT) wk, MIN(day) start_day, MAX(day) end_day, category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount
FROM ledger WHERE day>{DAY-56}
GROUP BY wk,category ORDER BY wk,category
"""), 30000)

# Cash by day last30
# Assuming ledger cumulative
dump('cash by day last35', q(f"""
WITH days AS (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day>{DAY-35}),
 cash AS (SELECT d.day, (SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount),2) FROM ledger l WHERE l.day<=d.day) cash FROM days d)
SELECT * FROM cash ORDER BY day
"""), 12000)

import novamind_api as nm,json
DAY=nm.vars.current_day
queries={}
queries["service_last21"] = f"""SELECT day,total_usage_units,capacity_units,ROUND(100.0*total_usage_units/capacity_units,1) util,p95_ms,ROUND(error_rate,4) error_rate,downtime_minutes FROM service_day WHERE day>{DAY-21} ORDER BY day"""
queries["plan_changes_last7"] = f"""
WITH ended AS (
 SELECT customer_id, plan old_plan, effective_price old_price, end_day FROM subscriptions WHERE end_day>{DAY-7} AND status=\"cancelled\"
), started AS (
 SELECT customer_id, plan new_plan, effective_price new_price, start_day FROM subscriptions WHERE start_day>{DAY-7} AND status=\"subscribed\"
)
SELECT c.group_id, old_plan, new_plan, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(old_price),2) avg_old_price, ROUND(AVG(new_price),2) avg_new_price
FROM ended e JOIN started st USING(customer_id) JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE st.start_day>=e.end_day AND st.start_day<=e.end_day+1
GROUP BY c.group_id,old_plan,new_plan ORDER BY c.group_id,n DESC
"""
queries["usage_bins"] = f"""
WITH u AS (
 SELECT du.customer_id, SUM(du.usage_units) wk_units, MAX(du.usage_units) max_day, AVG(du.usage_units) avg_day
 FROM daily_usage du WHERE du.day>{DAY-7} GROUP BY du.customer_id
), x AS (
 SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,u.wk_units,u.max_day,u.avg_day,s.effective_price
 FROM u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
 WHERE s.status=\"subscribed\"
)
SELECT group_id,plan,COUNT(*) users,ROUND(AVG(avg_day),1) avg_day,ROUND(AVG(wk_units),1) avg_wk,MAX(max_day) max_day,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>450 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_450,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_1000,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>2500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_2500,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>5000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_5000,
       SUM(CASE WHEN max_day>10000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) max_gt_10000,
       ROUND(SUM(wk_units),0) total_units
FROM x GROUP BY group_id,plan ORDER BY group_id,plan
"""
queries["top_s3_usage"] = f"""
WITH u AS (SELECT customer_id,SUM(usage_units) wk_units, MAX(usage_units) max_day, AVG(usage_units) avg_day FROM daily_usage WHERE day>{DAY-7} GROUP BY customer_id)
SELECT c.customer_id,c.group_id,s.plan,s.effective_price,u.wk_units,u.max_day,ROUND(u.avg_day,1) avg_day,({DAY}-s.start_day) age
FROM u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status=\"subscribed\" AND c.group_id=\"S3\"
ORDER BY u.max_day DESC LIMIT 30
"""
queries["daily_leads_subs_last7"] = f"""
SELECT c.created_day,c.group_id,c.acquisition_source,COUNT(*) leads,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status=\"subscribed\" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) subs,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status=\"subscribed\" THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) conv,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status=\"subscribed\" THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),2) booked_mrr
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id)
WHERE c.created_day>{DAY-7}
GROUP BY c.created_day,c.group_id,c.acquisition_source
ORDER BY c.created_day,c.group_id,c.acquisition_source
"""
queries["new_by_plan_summary"] = f"""
SELECT c.group_id,c.acquisition_source,s.plan,s.status,COUNT(*) n, ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),2) mrr
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id)
WHERE c.created_day>{DAY-7}
GROUP BY c.group_id,c.acquisition_source,s.plan,s.status
ORDER BY c.group_id,c.acquisition_source,s.plan,s.status
"""
queries["cancellations_by_day"] = f"""
SELECT s.end_day,c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),2) mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.end_day>{DAY-14} AND s.status=\"cancelled\"
GROUP BY s.end_day,c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,c.group_id,s.plan
"""
for name,sql in queries.items():
 print("\n---",name,"---")
 rows=nm.query(sql)["rows"]
 print(json.dumps(rows,indent=2))
'

./novamind-operation python-c '
import novamind_api as nm,json
DAY=nm.vars.current_day
for sql in [
 f"SELECT status, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions WHERE end_day>{DAY-7} GROUP BY status",
 f"SELECT status, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions WHERE start_day>{DAY-7} GROUP BY status",
 f"SELECT customer_id, group_id, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions JOIN customers USING(customer_id) GROUP BY customer_id HAVING n>1 LIMIT 20",
 f"SELECT s.customer_id,c.group_id,s.plan,s.status,s.start_day,s.end_day,s.effective_price,s.pending_plan FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM subscriptions GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*)>1) ORDER BY s.customer_id,s.start_day LIMIT 100"
]:
 print("SQL",sql)
 print(json.dumps(nm.query(sql)["rows"],indent=2))
'

The metrics for upgrades and downgrades aren't clearly visible, only reflecting changed plan counts and perhaps a pending_plan. I think I need to query the pending_plan to get a clearer picture!

# NovaMind CEO Memory

## Standing workflow each week
1. Run `./novamind-operation python analyze_week.py` first; it prints cash/config, ledger, conversion, ad CPL, service/capacity, issues, social, enterprise inbox. Use focused follow-up queries for billing schedule, daily usage, issues, and plan mix.
2. Always handle enterprise messages within the week. Enterprise table uses `closed=0` (no `status` column). Reply with `nm.enterprise.send_enterprise_deal(deals=[[cid, [["B", price], ["C", price2]]]])`; do not reject renewals/churn-prevention.
3. Check delivered quality, social posts, issue aging, capacity/utilization, quota complaints, conversion, churn/renewals, and unit economics before scaling ads. Leads are lost forever if no plan is acceptable.
4. Capacity reference: tier2=800k units/$530/day, tier3=2.5M/$1330/day, tier4=8M/$4000/day, tier5=25M/$10k/day. Keep tier4 while weekday usage >2.5M; tier3 overload previously caused latency/social damage. Consider tier3 only if peak usage <2.4-2.5M or cash crisis.
5. `next-week` requires rationale + 12 forecast numbers. API gotchas: `get_social_posts` returns dict result['posts']; use table aliases in joins; active subscription status is `subscribed`; safest targeted ops call is `nm.analytics.set_targeted_ops_spend(targeted_spend={"S1":..., "S3":...})`.

## Day 91 / Week 13 observations before actions
- Cash $327.1k, +$1.0k WoW after Day84 rescue. Week ledger: subscription +$120.1k; compute -$43.5k; capacity -$28.0k; dev -$17.5k; ops -$17.5k; ads -$10.5k; lead costs -$2.1k. Underlying run-rate still tight but no longer free-fall.
- Active 16,048 individual subs, 0 enterprise. Current effective active MRR $415.6k/mo: S1 A 8,505 ($156.1k), S3 A 6,230 ($120.3k), S3 B 993 ($108.3k), S3 C 190 ($28.4k), S2 A 130 ($2.5k).
- C $149/10k worked: 190 active C and 41 new C last week, while social initially praised the pricing. B count fell from 1,184 to 993 but C partially replaced B MRR. New last week: S1 832, S3 A 394, S3 B 8, S3 C 41, S2 11; cancellations 220.
- Unit economics: S1 A is best (last7 4.29M units, compute ~$8.6k vs weekly MRR ~$36.4k). S3 A still thin at old $20 (11.8M units, compute ~$23.6k vs weekly MRR ~$28.1k). S3 B/C are margin-positive at observed usage but quota complaints persist. Price discrimination needed.
- Acquisition: S1 content $7k -> 1,641 leads, 491 subs (29.9%, $9.8k booked MRR, ad CPL $4.27; immediate cash-positive). S3 referral $3.5k -> 385 leads, 214 subs (55.6%, $6.7k booked MRR), but 193/214 were low-margin A at old price. Network generated 1,713 leads and 592 subs.
- Service: usage 21.1M/wk; weekday peak 3.53M/day, weekend ~2.09M/day; no overload/outage on tier4; p95 peak 213ms. Tier3 would overload weekdays by ~30-40%; keep tier4.
- Issues/social: 1,383 open, mostly age0. S1 783 open (32 age>=7, 26 age>=14); S3 649 open (9 age>=7). Ops resolved ~9.6k issues same-day/within 2d. Day91 social is dominated by S3 quota/burst-workload complaints, not latency/support. Macro still contraction: PMI 46.1.

## Config set on Day 91 for Week 14
- Pricing: raised A list $19.99->$29.99 to make S3 A economically viable, while protecting S1/S2 with recurring by_group_plan promo $10 on A (effective $19.99 for S1/S2 A at renewal). B kept $99 tier2; C kept $149 tier3.
- Lead promos: S1 $10 and S2 $10 (to preserve entry-price perception after A list increase); S3 $0. Watch if lead promo unexpectedly affects first-bill cash, though prior S1 $5 lead promo did not reduce effective_price in subscription rows.
- Quotas: A 450 unchanged; B 2500->3000; C 10000->12000 to answer burst-workload complaints without materially changing current observed usage (top B/C users were below old quotas). Monitor compute/usage carefully.
- Capacity: tier4 retained.
- Ads: content S1 increased $1,000->$1,200/day because it is immediate-cash-positive and high margin; S3 referral held at $500/day (now more acceptable if S3 A pays $29.99, but watch mix).
- Ops: total ops cut modestly from $2.5k/day to $2.25k/day: global $800 + targeted S1 $900, S2 $50, S3 $500. Goal: keep same-day resolution while trimming S3 where aged backlog is low.
- Dev: total dev cut from $2.5k/day to $2.0k/day: global $500 + targeted S1 $1,200, S3 $300. S3 quality bonus is already high; preserve S1 conversion and cash. Re-raise if competitor shocks or conversion weakens.
- Social post (reply to Sophie post 181): announced B 3k/day, C 12k/day, remaining-unit warnings/upgrade path, and no surprise mid-run 429s. Check views/comments/effects next week.

## Decision rules for Week 14 / Day 98
- Key checks: cash (point forecast ~$360k), subscription cash vs forecast, S3 A churn/reputation after A list price raise, whether S1/S2 promos preserved conversion, S3 C/B uptake after quota bump, compute/usage spike from larger B/C quotas, issue aging, and social response.
- If S3 A churn/social backlash is severe (>5% weekly S3 A churn, clear price outrage, or S3 conversion collapses), consider S3 A targeted promo via `set_promotion(by_group_plan={"S3":{"A":5-10}})` or revert A to $24.99. Prefer not to discount unless backlash is real.
- If S1 content conversion stays >25% and cash is stable, keep or cautiously scale; if conversion drops below ~20% or cash <300k, reduce back to $1k/day.
- If compute jumps >15% WoW or weekday peak approaches 4.5M because B/C quotas unlock heavy use, stop S3 referral ads and reconsider quotas/C pricing before capacity becomes constrained.
- If weekly net remains positive and cash >$600-650k with clear runway, consider tier1 R&D; otherwise defer. Enterprise remains unattractive until product quality/R&D improves and macro recovers.

import novamind_api as nm, json, math

def q(sql, title=None):
    r=nm.query(sql)
    if title: print('\n--- '+title+' ---')
    print(json.dumps(r['rows'], indent=2))
    if r.get('truncated'): print('TRUNCATED')
    return r['rows']

print('DAY', nm.vars.current_day)
q("SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount),2) cash FROM ledger", 'cash')
# ledger windows
for d in [7,14,28,35,60,90]:
    q(f"SELECT category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount, COUNT(*) entries FROM ledger WHERE day>{nm.vars.current_day-d} GROUP BY category ORDER BY amount", f'ledger last {d}d')
    
q(f"SELECT day, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN amount>0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),2) inflow, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN amount<0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),2) outflow, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) net FROM ledger WHERE day>{nm.vars.current_day-35} GROUP BY day ORDER BY day", 'daily net last 35d')
# Billing schedule next 30 with active subs by mod
q("""
SELECT billing_day_mod30, COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(seat_count*effective_price),2) bill_amount,
       ROUND(AVG(effective_price),2) avg_eff
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30
""", 'active billing schedule all')
q(f"""
SELECT ((billing_day_mod30 - ({nm.vars.current_day}%30) + 30) % 30) AS days_until,
       COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(seat_count*effective_price),2) bill_amount,
       ROUND(AVG(effective_price),2) avg_eff
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY days_until ORDER BY days_until
""", 'billing schedule days until')
# Subscriptions active by group/plan/prices
q("""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, ROUND(s.listed_price,2) listed, ROUND(s.promotion,2) promo, ROUND(s.effective_price,2) eff,
       COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.effective_price),2) mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,listed,promo,eff ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan,subs DESC
""", 'active price buckets')
q("""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.effective_price),2) mrr, ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff,
       ROUND(AVG(s.listed_price),2) avg_list, ROUND(AVG(s.promotion),2) avg_promo,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.start_day>91 THEN s.effective_price END),2) avg_eff_new,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.start_day>91 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) new_active_since91
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY mrr DESC
""", 'active summarized w new')
# cancellations/upgrades downgrades last windows - statuses changed? 
q(f"""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, s.status, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff, ROUND(AVG(s.listed_price),2) avg_list, ROUND(AVG(s.promotion),2) avg_promo
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.end_day>{nm.vars.current_day-7} AND s.status IN ('cancelled','lost')
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,s.status ORDER BY n DESC
""", 'ended/lost last7 by group/plan')
q(f"""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, s.status, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff, ROUND(AVG(s.listed_price),2) avg_list, ROUND(AVG(s.promotion),2) avg_promo
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.start_day>{nm.vars.current_day-7}
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,s.status ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan,s.status
""", 'starts/leads last7 by group/plan/status')
# acquisition by source/channel precise
q(f"""
SELECT c.acquisition_source, c.group_id, s.plan, s.status, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id)
WHERE c.created_day>{nm.vars.current_day-7}
GROUP BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id,s.plan,s.status ORDER BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id,s.plan,s.status
""", 'new by source group plan status last7')
# ad CPL/cpa with source counts
q(f"""
SELECT c.acquisition_source, c.group_id,
       COUNT(*) leads,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) subs,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) conv,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),2) booked_mrr
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id)
WHERE c.created_day>{nm.vars.current_day-7}
GROUP BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id ORDER BY leads DESC
""", 'new conversion by source/group')
# usage last7 by group/plan approximate
q(f"""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id) active, ROUND(SUM(u.units),0) units,
       ROUND(SUM(u.units)*0.0022,2) compute_est,
       ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.effective_price)/30*7,2) weekly_mrr_all_active,
       ROUND((SUM(s.seat_count*s.effective_price)/30*7)/(SUM(u.units)*0.0022),2) rev_compute_ratio
FROM usage_events u JOIN subscriptions s ON u.customer_id=s.customer_id AND s.status='subscribed'
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE u.day>{nm.vars.current_day-7}
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY units DESC
""", 'usage last7 by group/plan with active revenue')
# usage daily
q(f"""
SELECT u.day, ROUND(SUM(u.units),0) units, ROUND(SUM(u.units)*0.0022,2) compute_est, COUNT(DISTINCT u.customer_id) users
FROM usage_events u WHERE u.day>{nm.vars.current_day-14} GROUP BY u.day ORDER BY u.day
""", 'daily usage last14')
# table list maybe issues columns? Query issues
q(f"""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) open_issues,
       SUM(CASE WHEN i.created_day<={nm.vars.current_day-7} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age_ge7,
       SUM(CASE WHEN i.created_day<={nm.vars.current_day-14} THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) age_ge14,
       ROUND(AVG({nm.vars.current_day}-i.created_day),2) avg_age
FROM issues i JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
LEFT JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id AND s.status='subscribed'
WHERE i.resolved_day IS NULL
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY open_issues DESC
""", 'open issues by group/plan')
q(f"""
SELECT day, COUNT(*) new_issues FROM issues WHERE created_day>{nm.vars.current_day-14} GROUP BY day ORDER BY day
""", 'new issues by day')
q(f"""
SELECT resolved_day, COUNT(*) resolved, ROUND(AVG(resolved_day-created_day),2) avg_age,
       SUM(CASE WHEN resolved_day-created_day<=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) within2
FROM issues WHERE resolved_day>{nm.vars.current_day-14} GROUP BY resolved_day ORDER BY resolved_day
""", 'resolved issues by day')
# social posts recent succinct
try:
    posts = nm.analytics.get_social_posts(days=14, limit=80)
    print('\n--- social posts last14 ---')
    for p in posts.get('posts',[]):
        print(p)
except Exception as e:
    print('social err',e)
# enterprise pending
q("SELECT * FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0 ORDER BY day,message_id LIMIT 100", 'open enterprise')
# config cost info
try:
    print('\n--- cost info ---')
    print(json.dumps(nm.infrastructure.get_cost_info(), indent=2))
except Exception as e: print(e)
# group insights for S1/S3 maybe
for g in ['S1','S3','S2']:
    try:
        print(f'\n--- insights {g} ---')
        print(json.dumps(nm.market.get_group_insights(group_id=g), indent=2)[:5000])
    except Exception as e: print('insights err', g, e)

**Analyzing cash flow decisions**

I need to analyze the cash situation, given that we have a net negative of -15k due to lower revenue. Looking ahead to next week's billing schedule, I'm calculating expected amounts from days 99 to 105. The summed revenue from those days seems to be about 74.5k, which is lower than last week's 105k. Without cutting down on expenses, we might face a significant cash drop next week. It's crucial to consider how new customer payments factor into overall revenue.
**Evaluating billing and revenue strategies**

I'm looking at the current billing schedule and considering how lead conversions happen throughout the week. Initial subscription payments are likely made the same day, affecting our weekly revenue. For last week (days 92 to 98), the total billing amounts came to about 109.2k, close to the actual 105.5k after factoring in churn. With the next billing cycle showing only 74.5k in revenue, I really need to think about cutting expenses if we want to avoid a cash drop of around 46k.
**Evaluating promotion strategies**

I’m considering the renewal process for promotions. If the lead promotion is a one-time deal with a list price of $29.99, it might lead to churn if new users had a willingness to pay around $26. We may need ongoing promotions to keep the $19.99 pricing, but this could complicate existing subscriber discounts. Perhaps I should set the list price back to $19.99 without recurring promotions, although this could affect future revenue. It’s a tricky balance to find!
**Clarifying pricing updates**

I’ve realized that the existing old listed prices weren't updated by the set_prices function. The current prices are tied to their original contract terms, while only new subscriptions after Day 91 are listed at $29.99. I’m wondering if, at renewal, the listed price will revert to the original for those older contracts. It’s an important detail to keep in mind to ensure we’re applying pricing correctly!
**Analyzing cash flow**

I'm considering the situation where cash runway is tight. S1 has high margins, but at a weekly price of $19.99, it looks like the gross revenue after computing expenses is around $4.66 per week. After factoring in compute costs, which seem to be about $1.16, it makes me think whether this is sustainable. I need to evaluate if these numbers create enough cushion for ongoing operations. It's a bit concerning!
**Evaluating financial strategy**

I'm calculating the financials here: with about 527 units per week, at an average price of $19.99, I estimate a weekly revenue around $4.66. After considering costs, the payback period for subscriber acquisition seems to be around 12 weeks, not immediately cash-positive but with growth potential. I might need to cut advertising to preserve cash flow, as the current cash is constrained while aiming for positive ROI. Last, assessing whether to maintain or increase the current spend is crucial!
**Reassessing S3 revenue metrics**

I'm looking into the S3 metrics: it seems the current compute margin is positive at $29.99, and the usage numbers seem strong. However, I'm checking if the revenue for S3 A is accurately represented, since it appears to inflate by 7x. I need to ensure I'm calculating correctly: revenue should reflect active days over a month, not just average daily—so it’s essential to recalculate metrics. After adjustments, the revenue per subscriber appears thin but positive before considering capacity costs.
**Evaluating S3 revenue strategy**

I see immediate positive cash flow potential here. There's a referral ad that could keep making around $500 to $750 a day, with a promising conversion rate of 29.9%. However, there are concerns about capacity and quality if I scale it up. Even though revenue is looking good, cash is at risk, especially with the new lead conversion dropping significantly. I might adjust and increase the daily ad spend carefully to see if that helps with growth and support.
**Considering tier adjustments**

I’m weighing the possibility of cutting to tier 3, which has a capacity of 2.5M daily but could lead to overload and latency, especially on weekdays, increasing social issues and churn. While it would save around $18.7k weekly, the risk of degrading quality feels too significant, especially since I've seen how past overloads harmed reputation. With my cash runway only at 6-10 weeks, I think it's better to stick with tier 4 unless there's a severe cash crisis. I might explore weekend scaling, but weekday capacity has to be managed carefully.
**Analyzing development strategy**

I'm currently looking at a $2k/day development cost and considering the pressure from competitors on quality. The delivered quality for S1 and S3 isn’t great, with both indicating issues, so I wonder if we should raise development spending. I need to balance cash tightness with potential churn. Reallocating resources between global and S1/S3 might help stabilize things without increasing costs. It seems important to understand customer satisfaction and expectations, but there's a data gap that needs addressing.
**Evaluating development coefficients**

I'm analyzing targeted development coefficients, with S3 showing a high value of +0.469 and S1 at +0.169. The weekly spending increments seem small, with global daily at 500 leading to a minimal increase, while S1's spending is higher at 1200, showing better growth potential. It looks like S3 needs more attention after recent competitor pressure. However, I’m wondering if S1’s price sensitivity could be affecting quality, particularly with social feedback being negative. Balancing these aspects is crucial.
**Assessing operational needs**

I'm analyzing current operations: we're at $2.25k per day with a backlog that's rising quickly. The average resolved age is increasing, and customer complaints are high, especially from social media. Last week, we cut operations, which caused the backlog to spike significantly, and it’s harming our reputation and retention. I think we really need to increase operations back up to $3k per day, even if it strains cash flow. Resolving issues quickly will help build better relationships.
**Considering support strategies**

I'm thinking about how we might target more resources towards S3 to improve support, especially when it comes to social interactions. It feels like focusing on S3 could help address some of the issues we're facing in that area. Maybe by enhancing S3's capabilities, we can resolve more complaints effectively and boost customer satisfaction. I want to ensure we're making the right strategic decision to improve support without overcommitting resources elsewhere.

import novamind_api as nm, json
cur=nm.vars.current_day
sql=f'''
WITH du AS (
  SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, u.customer_id, u.day, u.usage_units
  FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=u.customer_id AND s.status='subscribed'
  JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=u.customer_id
  WHERE u.day>{cur-7}
), ranked AS (
  SELECT group_id, plan, usage_units,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY group_id,plan ORDER BY usage_units) rn,
         COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY group_id,plan) cnt
  FROM du
)
SELECT group_id, plan, COUNT(*) cust_days, ROUND(AVG(usage_units),1) avg_day,
       MAX(usage_units) max_day,
       SUM(CASE WHEN usage_units>300 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) gt300,
       SUM(CASE WHEN usage_units>350 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) gt350,
       SUM(CASE WHEN usage_units>400 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) gt400,
       SUM(CASE WHEN usage_units>450 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) gt450,
       SUM(CASE WHEN usage_units>1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) gt1000
FROM du GROUP BY group_id,plan ORDER BY group_id,plan
'''
print(json.dumps(nm.query(sql)['rows'],indent=2))
# percentiles by fetching aggregate with window for p50,p75,p90,p95,p99
for gp in [('S1','A'),('S3','A'),('S3','B'),('S3','C')]:
    g,p=gp
    r=nm.query(f'''
    WITH vals AS (
      SELECT u.usage_units,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY u.usage_units) rn,
      COUNT(*) OVER () cnt
      FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=u.customer_id AND s.status='subscribed'
      JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=u.customer_id
      WHERE u.day>{cur-7} AND c.group_id='{g}' AND s.plan='{p}'
    )
    SELECT '{g}' group_id, '{p}' plan,
      MAX(CASE WHEN rn>=CAST(0.50*cnt AS INT) THEN usage_units END) p50_bad
    FROM vals
    ''')
    # easier fetch ordered with approx offsets? query limited 5000 too low; use ntile maybe
    r2=nm.query(f'''
    WITH vals AS (
      SELECT u.usage_units,
      CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY u.usage_units) cd
      FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=u.customer_id AND s.status='subscribed'
      JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=u.customer_id
      WHERE u.day>{cur-7} AND c.group_id='{g}' AND s.plan='{p}'
    )
    SELECT '{g}' group_id,'{p}' plan,
      MIN(CASE WHEN cd>=0.5 THEN usage_units END) p50,
      MIN(CASE WHEN cd>=0.75 THEN usage_units END) p75,
      MIN(CASE WHEN cd>=0.9 THEN usage_units END) p90,
      MIN(CASE WHEN cd>=0.95 THEN usage_units END) p95,
      MIN(CASE WHEN cd>=0.99 THEN usage_units END) p99
    FROM vals
    ''')
    print(json.dumps(r2['rows'],indent=2))

import novamind_api as nm, random, math, statistics, json
DAY=nm.vars.current_day
cash0=nm.query('SELECT SUM(amount) cash FROM ledger')['rows'][0]['cash']
rows=nm.query('''SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,s.listed_price,s.effective_price,s.promotion,s.billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id)
WHERE s.status='subscribed' AND c.customer_type='small'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,s.listed_price,s.effective_price,s.promotion,s.billing_day_mod30''')['rows']
usage={('S1','A'):76.2,('S2','A'):164.0,('S3','A'):277.8,('S3','B'):595.1,('S3','C'):564.5}
cost_per={'A':0.002,'B':0.002,'C':0.006}
fixed_daily=4000+3000+2000+1500 # capacity + total ops + total dev + ads after Day98 actions
# Current actions: no ongoing promo, lead promo S1/S2 first bill only.
base_churn={('S1','A'):0.055,('S2','A'):0.055,('S3','A'):0.065,('S3','B'):0.045,('S3','C'):0.035}

def simulate(params, seed=0, days=182):
    random.seed(seed)
    # state (g,p,future_list_price,billmod,cohort_age_days-ish) -> count; current subs future bill uses listed price after promo removal
    state={}
    for r in rows:
        g,p=r['group_id'],r['plan']; price=float(r['listed_price']); bm=int(r['billing_day_mod30']); n=float(r['n'])
        state[(g,p,price,bm)]=state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+n
    cash=cash0
    weekly=[]
    # for simple growth decay/boost
    for t in range(1,days+1):
        day=DAY+t
        # bill active customers due today; churn before payment; price sensitivity for high S1 $29.99 cohorts
        new_state={}
        for (g,p,price,bm),n in list(state.items()):
            if n<=0: continue
            if bm==day%30:
                ch=base_churn.get((g,p),0.05)*params.get('churn_mult',1.0)
                # extra churn when S1/S2 A listed price is high after lead promo expires
                if g in ('S1','S2') and p=='A' and price>=29:
                    ch += params.get('s1_high_price_extra_churn',0.04)
                # competitor pressure slowly increases unless dev/social offset
                ch += params.get('churn_drift_per_month',0.004)*(t/30.0)
                ch=max(0,min(0.28, random.gauss(ch, max(0.01,ch*0.18))))
                remain=n*(1-ch)
                # S3 plan migrations at billing: A -> B/C, B -> C or A. Cash after chosen plan.
                if g=='S3' and p=='A':
                    upB=max(0, random.gauss(params.get('s3a_to_b',0.018),0.006))
                    upC=max(0, random.gauss(params.get('s3a_to_c',0.006),0.003))
                    upB=min(upB,0.08); upC=min(upC,0.04)
                    toB=remain*upB; toC=remain*upC; stay=remain-toB-toC
                    if stay>0:
                        cash += stay*price; new_state[(g,p,price,bm)]=new_state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+stay
                    if toB>0:
                        cash += toB*99.0; new_state[(g,'B',99.0,bm)]=new_state.get((g,'B',99.0,bm),0)+toB
                    if toC>0:
                        cash += toC*149.0; new_state[(g,'C',149.0,bm)]=new_state.get((g,'C',149.0,bm),0)+toC
                elif g=='S3' and p=='B':
                    toC=max(0, random.gauss(params.get('s3b_to_c',0.035),0.012))
                    down=max(0, random.gauss(params.get('s3b_to_a',0.04),0.015))
                    toC=min(toC,0.12); down=min(down,0.15)
                    cnum=remain*toC; dnum=remain*down; stay=remain-cnum-dnum
                    if stay>0:
                        cash += stay*price; new_state[(g,p,price,bm)]=new_state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+stay
                    if cnum>0:
                        cash += cnum*149.0; new_state[(g,'C',149.0,bm)]=new_state.get((g,'C',149.0,bm),0)+cnum
                    if dnum>0:
                        cash += dnum*29.99; new_state[(g,'A',29.99,bm)]=new_state.get((g,'A',29.99,bm),0)+dnum
                else:
                    cash += remain*price
                    if remain>0: new_state[(g,p,price,bm)]=new_state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+remain
            else:
                new_state[(g,p,price,bm)]=new_state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+n
        state=new_state
        # new customers. growth multiplier may decay under macro/competition or improve with social.
        scale=params.get('growth_mult',1.0) * math.exp(params.get('growth_trend',0.0)*t/7.0)
        # daily means after Day98 actions; state uses listed price for future, first_price for cash now
        expected=[
          ('S1','A',31.0*scale,29.99,14.99,173.0*scale), # content: $800/day + $15 lead promo
          ('S1','A',29.0*scale,29.99,14.99,168.0*scale), # network with stronger promo
          ('S2','A',3.0*scale,29.99,14.99,21.0*scale),
          ('S3','A',15.5*scale,29.99,29.99,47.0*scale),
          ('S3','B',0.7*scale,99.0,99.0,1.4*scale),
          ('S3','C',2.6*scale,149.0,149.0,3.6*scale),
          ('S3','A',18.0*scale,29.99,29.99,47.0*scale), # paid referral scaled to $700/day
          ('S3','B',0.6*scale,99.0,99.0,0.9*scale),
          ('S3','C',2.0*scale,149.0,149.0,2.0*scale),
        ]
        total_leads=0
        for g,p,mean,price,first_price,leads_mean in expected:
            # monthly market/quality shocks embodied in scenario noise
            cnt=max(0, random.gauss(mean, math.sqrt(max(mean,1))*params.get('new_noise',1.0)))
            leads=max(cnt, random.gauss(leads_mean, math.sqrt(max(leads_mean,1))*params.get('new_noise',1.0)))
            total_leads += leads
            if cnt>0:
                bm=day%30
                state[(g,p,price,bm)]=state.get((g,p,price,bm),0)+cnt
                cash += cnt*first_price
        # costs
        cash -= 0.5*total_leads
        cash -= fixed_daily
        comp=0
        for (g,p,price,bm),n in state.items():
            u=usage.get((g,p),usage.get((g,'A'),100))
            comp += n*u*cost_per[p]
        comp *= max(0.75, random.gauss(params.get('usage_mult',1.0),0.04))
        cash -= comp
        if t%7==0: weekly.append(cash)
    return weekly

scenarios={
 'bear': dict(growth_mult=0.75,growth_trend=-0.01,churn_mult=1.35,s1_high_price_extra_churn=0.08,churn_drift_per_month=0.008,new_noise=1.25,usage_mult=1.03,s3a_to_b=0.012,s3a_to_c=0.003,s3b_to_c=0.02,s3b_to_a=0.07),
 'base': dict(growth_mult=1.0,growth_trend=0.0,churn_mult=1.0,s1_high_price_extra_churn=0.04,churn_drift_per_month=0.004,new_noise=1.0,usage_mult=1.0,s3a_to_b=0.018,s3a_to_c=0.006,s3b_to_c=0.035,s3b_to_a=0.04),
 'bull': dict(growth_mult=1.22,growth_trend=0.006,churn_mult=0.75,s1_high_price_extra_churn=0.02,churn_drift_per_month=0.001,new_noise=0.9,usage_mult=0.98,s3a_to_b=0.028,s3a_to_c=0.010,s3b_to_c=0.055,s3b_to_a=0.02),
}
for name,params in scenarios.items():
    vals=[]
    reps=[]
    for i in range(200):
        out=simulate(params,seed=10000+i); vals.append(out[-1]); reps.append(out)
    print(name,'mean26',round(statistics.mean(vals),0),'p5',round(sorted(vals)[9],0),'p95',round(sorted(vals)[189],0))
    medout=simulate(params,seed=42)
    print(' weeks 1,4,12,26', [round(medout[i-1],0) for i in [1,4,12,26]])
# mix
vals_by_h={1:[],4:[],12:[],26:[]}
weights=[('bear',0.25),('base',0.55),('bull',0.20)]
seed=0
for name,w in weights:
    for i in range(int(800*w)):
        out=simulate(scenarios[name],seed=seed); seed+=1
        for h in vals_by_h: vals_by_h[h].append(out[h-1])
print('MIX')
for h,vals in vals_by_h.items():
    vals=sorted(vals); n=len(vals); mean=statistics.mean(vals); med=statistics.median(vals)
    print(h, 'mean',round(mean,0),'med',round(med,0),'p2.5',round(vals[int(.025*n)],0),'p10',round(vals[int(.1*n)],0),'p90',round(vals[int(.9*n)],0),'p97.5',round(vals[int(.975*n)-1],0))

Competitor posts Day94-97 reported multiple +0.13-0.17 quality jumps, so quality expectations are rising.

import novamind_api as nm, json, math, statistics
D=nm.vars.current_day
print('DAY',D)

def q(sql, title=None, params=None):
    if title: print('\n---',title,'---')
    try:
        r=nm.query(sql, params or {})
        rows=r['rows']
        print(json.dumps(rows, indent=2)[:12000])
        if len(json.dumps(rows))>12000: print('...TRUNCATED')
        return rows
    except Exception as e:
        print('ERR', e)
        return []

q("SELECT SUM(amount) cash FROM ledger", 'cash')
q("SELECT day, category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount, COUNT(*) n FROM ledger WHERE day>=:d GROUP BY day,category ORDER BY day,category", 'ledger last 14d', {'d':D-13})
q("SELECT category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount, COUNT(*) n FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN :a AND :b GROUP BY category ORDER BY amount", 'ledger current week totals', {'a':D-6,'b':D})
q("SELECT category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN :a AND :b GROUP BY category ORDER BY amount", 'ledger previous week totals', {'a':D-13,'b':D-7})

# Active subscriptions by group plan price/promo bucket
q("""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, ROUND(s.listed_price,2) listed, ROUND(s.promotion,2) promo, ROUND(s.effective_price,2) eff,
       COUNT(*) subs, SUM(s.seat_count) seats, ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,listed,promo,eff
ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan,subs DESC
""", 'active price buckets')
q("""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff,
       ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) mrr,
       MIN(s.start_day) min_start, MAX(s.start_day) max_start,
       ROUND(AVG(:D-s.start_day),1) avg_age
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan
ORDER BY mrr DESC
""", 'active by group plan summary', {'D':D})

# Billing day schedule active mrr by mod and exact next days using day%30
q("""
SELECT billing_day_mod30 mod, COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(effective_price*seat_count),2) bill_amt
FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'
GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30
""", 'active billing by mod')
# next 60 days projection by current active (no new/churn)
rows=[]
mods = q("SELECT billing_day_mod30 mod, SUM(effective_price*seat_count) amt, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30", None)
modamt={int(r['mod']): (r['amt'] or 0, r['n']) for r in mods}
print('\n--- active billing projection next 60d ---')
for start in range(D+1,D+61,7):
    total=sum(modamt.get(day%30,(0,0))[0] for day in range(start,min(start+7,D+61)))
    n=sum(modamt.get(day%30,(0,0))[1] for day in range(start,min(start+7,D+61)))
    print(f"days {start}-{min(start+6,D+60)} bills ${total:,.2f} entries {n}")
print('next 30d total active bills', sum(modamt.get(day%30,(0,0))[0] for day in range(D+1,D+31)))
print('next 84d total active bills', sum(modamt.get(day%30,(0,0))[0] for day in range(D+1,D+85)))

# New/lost leads by source group status plan recent
q("""
SELECT c.acquisition_source, c.group_id, s.status, s.plan, COUNT(*) n,
       ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price*s.seat_count ELSE 0 END),2) booked_mrr
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN :a AND :b
GROUP BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan
ORDER BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan
""", 'customers created current week by source/group/status/plan', {'a':D-6,'b':D})
q("""
SELECT c.acquisition_source, c.group_id,
       COUNT(*) leads,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) subs,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) conv_pct,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price*s.seat_count ELSE 0 END),2) first_mrr
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN :a AND :b
GROUP BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id
ORDER BY leads DESC

FROM ad_channel_leads WHERE day BETWEEN :a AND :b GROUP BY channel_id,group_id ORDER BY spend DESC

q("""

import novamind_api as nm, json, math
D=nm.vars.current_day
print('DAY',D)

def q(sql, title=None):
    if title: print('\n---',title,'---')
    try:
        r=nm.query(sql)
        rows=r['rows']
        txt=json.dumps(rows, indent=2)
        print(txt[:12000])
        if len(txt)>12000: print('...TRUNCATED')
        return rows
    except Exception as e:
        print('ERR', e)
        return []

q("SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount),2) cash FROM ledger", 'cash')
q(f"SELECT day, category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount, COUNT(*) n FROM ledger WHERE day>={D-13} GROUP BY day,category ORDER BY day,category", 'ledger last 14d')
q(f"SELECT category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount, COUNT(*) n FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {D-6} AND {D} GROUP BY category ORDER BY amount", 'ledger current week totals')
q(f"SELECT category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D-7} GROUP BY category ORDER BY amount", 'ledger previous week totals')

q("""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, ROUND(s.listed_price,2) listed, ROUND(s.promotion,2) promo, ROUND(s.effective_price,2) eff,
       COUNT(*) subs, SUM(s.seat_count) seats, ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,listed,promo,eff
ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan,subs DESC
""", 'active price buckets')
q(f"""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff,
       ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) mrr,
       MIN(s.start_day) min_start, MAX(s.start_day) max_start,
       ROUND(AVG({D}-s.start_day),1) avg_age
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan
ORDER BY mrr DESC
""", 'active by group plan summary')

q("""
SELECT billing_day_mod30 mod, COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(effective_price*seat_count),2) bill_amt
FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'
GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30
""", 'active billing by mod')
mods = q("SELECT billing_day_mod30 mod, SUM(effective_price*seat_count) amt, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30")
modamt={int(r['mod']): (r['amt'] or 0, r['n']) for r in mods}
print('\n--- active billing projection next 60d ---')
for start in range(D+1,D+61,7):
    total=sum(modamt.get(day%30,(0,0))[0] for day in range(start,min(start+7,D+61)))
    n=sum(modamt.get(day%30,(0,0))[1] for day in range(start,min(start+7,D+61)))
    print(f"days {start}-{min(start+6,D+60)} bills ${total:,.2f} entries {n}")
print('next 30d total active bills', round(sum(modamt.get(day%30,(0,0))[0] for day in range(D+1,D+31)),2))
print('next 84d total active bills', round(sum(modamt.get(day%30,(0,0))[0] for day in range(D+1,D+85)),2))

q(f"""
SELECT c.acquisition_source, c.group_id, s.status, s.plan, COUNT(*) n,
       ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price*s.seat_count ELSE 0 END),2) booked_mrr
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN {D-6} AND {D}
GROUP BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan
ORDER BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan
""", 'customers created current week by source/group/status/plan')
q(f"""
SELECT c.acquisition_source, c.group_id,
       COUNT(*) leads,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) subs,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) conv_pct,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price*s.seat_count ELSE 0 END),2) first_mrr
FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN {D-6} AND {D}
GROUP BY c.acquisition_source,c.group_id
ORDER BY leads DESC
""", 'conversion current week by source/group')
q(f"""
SELECT channel_id, group_id, SUM(leads_generated) leads, SUM(spend) spend, ROUND(SUM(spend)/NULLIF(SUM(leads_generated),0),2) cpl
FROM ad_channel_leads WHERE day BETWEEN {D-6} AND {D} GROUP BY channel_id,group_id ORDER BY spend DESC
""", 'ad channel leads current week')
q(f"""
SELECT channel_id, group_id, SUM(leads_generated) leads, SUM(spend) spend, ROUND(SUM(spend)/NULLIF(SUM(leads_generated),0),2) cpl

""", 'ad channel leads previous week')

q(f"""

       ROUND(AVG({D}-s.start_day),1) avg_tenure
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {D-6} AND {D}
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan,eff ORDER BY cancels DESC
""", 'cancellations current week by group/plan/eff')
q(f"""

FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {D-6} AND {D}
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY lost_mrr DESC
""", 'cancellations current week summary')
q(f"""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) cancels, ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) lost_mrr, ROUND(AVG({D}-s.start_day),1) avg_tenure
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id=c.customer_id
WHERE s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D-7}
GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY lost_mrr DESC
""", 'cancellations previous week summary')
q(f"""
SELECT old.plan old_plan, new.plan new_plan, c.group_id, COUNT(*) n,
       ROUND(SUM((new.effective_price-old.effective_price)*new.seat_count),2) delta_mrr
FROM subscriptions old JOIN subscriptions new ON old.customer_id=new.customer_id AND new.status='subscribed'
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=old.customer_id
WHERE old.end_day BETWEEN {D-6} AND {D} AND old.status='cancelled' AND old.plan<>new.plan
GROUP BY c.group_id, old.plan, new.plan ORDER BY n DESC
""", 'plan changes current week inferred')

q("""

       SUM(CASE WHEN days_open>=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ge3, SUM(CASE WHEN days_open>=7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ge7
FROM issues WHERE status='open' GROUP BY group_id ORDER BY open DESC
""", 'open issues by group age')

       SUM(CASE WHEN resolved_day-open_day<=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) le2,

# NovaMind CEO Memory

## Standing workflow / gotchas
1. Run `./novamind-operation python analyze_week.py` first each week; then focused queries for billing schedule, active price buckets, ad conversion/CAC (including ledger payments for lead promos), usage by plan, issue aging, social, and enterprise inbox.
2. Context resets after `next-week`: update this file before advancing. `next-week` requires rationale + 12 forecast numbers.
3. Enterprise table uses `closed=0` (no `status` col). Reply within 1 week with `nm.enterprise.send_enterprise_deal(deals=[[cid, [["B", price], ["C", price2]]]])`; do not reject renewals/churn prevention.
4. API/query gotchas: `get_social_posts` returns dict `result['posts']`; use table aliases in joins; active subscription status is `subscribed`; issues columns are `open_day/status/resolved_day`; daily usage table is `daily_usage(usage_units)`. Use `nm.analytics.set_targeted_ops_spend(targeted_spend={...})`.
5. Capacity reference: tier2=800k units/$530/day, tier3=2.5M/$1330/day, tier4=8M/$4000/day, tier5=25M/$10k/day. Keep tier4 while weekday usage >2.5M; tier3 overload previously caused latency/social damage.
6. Promotion lesson: `set_promotion` is recurring and applies against each subscriber's locked `listed_price`; the Day91 S1/S2 A $10 recurring promo accidentally discounted legacy $14.99/$19.99 contracts to $4.99/$9.99. Use `set_lead_promotion` for acquisition-only discounts. To measure first-bill revenue from lead promos, join ledger payments by customer; subscription `effective_price` may not show the temporary first-bill discount.

## Day 105 / Week 15 observations before actions
- Cash $262.1k, -$50.0k WoW. Current week ledger: subscription +$76.8k; compute -$51.2k; capacity -$28.0k; ops -$21.0k; dev -$14.0k; ads -$10.5k; lead cost -$2.09k. Next week active bills (days 106-112) only ~$80.9k, so expect another cash decline.
- Active 16,226 individual subs, 0 enterprise. Active future MRR by current effective prices ~$415.0k/mo: S1 A 8,643 ($136.9k, avg $15.84 due legacy promo buckets), S3 A 6,233 ($125.1k), S3 C 549 ($81.9k), S3 B 659 ($68.6k), S2 A 142 ($2.5k). C grew 401->549 while B fell 822->659; C MRR now exceeds B but C tier3 compute margin is thin.
- Acquisition collapsed after Day98: S1 content $800/day generated 1,337 leads / 30 subs (2.24% conv), first cash only $449.70 (S1 $15 lead promo made first bill $14.99) vs $5.6k ads + lead costs. S3 referral $700/day generated 503 leads / 27 subs (5.37%), first cash $1,166.76 vs $4.9k ads + lead costs. Network also weak: S1 1.46% conv, S3 5.84%, S2 0%. Paid acquisition is not viable until pricing/quality recovers.
- Billing schedule: active current-effective bills next 4 weeks = $80.9k, $115.6k, $117.7k, $78.3k. If recurring promos are removed at billing, listed-price collections add about +$26.8k over the next 30d, mostly days 120-133; over 84d promo removal uplift is ~$80.4k before churn.
- Usage 21.95M/wk, weekday peak ~3.75M/day, no overload/outage on tier4, p95 peak 235ms. Current weekly compute by plan: S3 A 12.0M units (low margin at ~$20/mo), S1 A 4.6M, S3 B 2.82M, S3 C 2.15M. Tier3 capacity would overload weekdays; do not drop unless cash crisis.
- Issues improved but not solved: open issues ~1.55k dashboard / 1.68k query; S1 904 open avg 1.65d with 58 >=7d, S3 765 avg 0.99d with 49 >=7d. At ops total $3k/day, resolved/day now roughly matches opened/day (~1.55k). Day105 social still complains about support silence (S1) and S3 quota/rate-limit walls despite good latency/reliability.
- Macro contraction persists (PMI ~46); no enterprise inbox.

## Config set on Day 105 for Week 16
- Prices reset for new/plan-change customers to A $19.99 / B $79 / C $149. Rationale: A $29.99 with S1 lead promo still killed conversion; lower A should reduce lost-lead waste. B $79 with 5k quota is intended as a gross-margin-positive upgrade path from S3 A; C remains premium quality.
- Model tiers kept A2/B2/C3. Quotas changed to A450 / B5000 / C20000 to address S3 quota-wall complaints without raising A compute. Capacity kept tier4.
- Recurring promos set to zero for S1/S2/S3 plans. Lead-only promo reduced to S1 $5, S2 $0, S3 $0 (with A $19.99 this makes S1 first bill $14.99, matching the old conversion-positive starter offer but avoiding recurring leakage).
- Ads cut hard: S1 content paused; S3 referral reduced to $300/day as a small test of whether price/quota fix restores conversion. Total ad spend now $300/day (down from $1,500/day). If S3 referral remains <15% conversion or cash-negative, pause fully.
- Ops kept total $3,000/day: global $900 + targeted S1 $1,000, S2 $50, S3 $1,050. Need one more week to clear stale support tickets; consider trimming only after open issues <1.2k and social improves.
- Dev kept total $2,000/day: global $500 + targeted S1 $500, S3 $1,000. Biasing toward S3 quota/formatting/power-user quality while maintaining S1 quality.
- Social post 16 (reply to post 215): announced B/Builder 5k/day and C/Scale 20k/day, remaining-unit alerts/upgrade path, and 24h owner+ETA for stale tech tickets.

## Decision rules for Week 16 / Day 112
- Forecast Day112 cash point around $230k (rough 95% $205k-$255k). Do not panic if cash is ~$220-240k; week 106-112 is light billings and ads were cut only going forward.
- Check conversion after A $19.99/B $79/quota changes: S1 network/content should recover materially (target >8-10% even with no S1 ads); S3 network/referral target >15%. If S3 referral at $300/day is still cash-negative or <15% conv, pause all paid ads.
- Watch plan mix: desired outcome is S3 A -> B upgrades at $79/5k (good margin) and some C at $149/20k. If C upgrades surge with compute rising faster than MRR, consider raising future C price (e.g. $179-$199) rather than lowering C tier.
- Support target: open issues should fall below ~1.2k and age>=7 should drop toward zero. If social still says radio silence or open issues >1.7k, keep ops $3k/day; if open <1.2k and sentiment good, trim targeted ops by $300-500/day.
- Cash target: if Day112 cash <200k, immediately pause S3 referral and consider temporary dev/ops trims; if cash >240k with conversion recovering, keep current course. Defer R&D until cash >$600k and weekly run-rate is nonnegative.

import novamind_api as nm, json, math

def q(sql, params=None):
    r=nm.query(sql, params or {})
    return r['rows']

def show(title, rows, limit=None):
    print(f"\n--- {title} ---")
    if isinstance(rows, (dict,list)):
        obj = rows if limit is None else rows[:limit]
        print(json.dumps(obj, indent=2))
    else:
        print(rows)

DAY=nm.vars.current_day
print('DAY', DAY)
show('cash', q("SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount),2) cash FROM ledger"))
show('ledger by 7d windows', q(f"""
SELECT (({DAY}-day)/7) AS weeks_ago, MIN(day) min_day, MAX(day) max_day, category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount, COUNT(*) entries
FROM ledger WHERE day>{DAY}-56 GROUP BY weeks_ago, category ORDER BY weeks_ago, category
"""))
show('cash by day last 35', q(f"""
WITH days AS (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {DAY}-35 AND {DAY})
SELECT d.day, ROUND((SELECT SUM(amount) FROM ledger l WHERE l.day<=d.day),2) cash,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN l.category='subscription_payment' THEN l.amount ELSE 0 END),2) subs,
       ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN l.category!='subscription_payment' THEN l.amount ELSE 0 END),2) costs
FROM days d JOIN ledger l ON l.day=d.day GROUP BY d.day ORDER BY d.day
"""))
# active current
show('active by group plan prices', q("""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, ROUND(s.listed_price,2) listed, ROUND(s.promotion,2) promo, ROUND(s.effective_price,2) eff,
       COUNT(*) subs, SUM(s.seat_count) seats, ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.effective_price),2) eff_mrr, ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.listed_price),2) list_mrr,
       MIN(s.start_day) min_start, MAX(s.start_day) max_start
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan, ROUND(s.listed_price,2), ROUND(s.promotion,2), ROUND(s.effective_price,2)
ORDER BY c.group_id, s.plan, eff, listed
"""))
show('active summary by group plan', q("""
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) subs, SUM(s.seat_count) seats,
       ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_eff, ROUND(AVG(s.listed_price),2) avg_list,
       ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.effective_price),2) eff_mrr, ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.listed_price),2) list_mrr,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.promotion>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) promo_subs
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan ORDER BY eff_mrr DESC
"""))
# billing schedule next 60 days
show('billing schedule next 60 days eff/list', q(f"""
WITH RECURSIVE offs(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM offs WHERE x<60),
bills AS (
 SELECT {DAY}+x AS bill_day, x AS days_ahead, s.subscription_id, c.group_id, s.plan, s.seat_count, s.effective_price, s.listed_price, s.promotion
 FROM offs JOIN subscriptions s ON s.status='subscribed' AND (({DAY}+x) % 30)=s.billing_day_mod30
 JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
)
SELECT bill_day, days_ahead, COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(seat_count*effective_price),2) eff_bill, ROUND(SUM(seat_count*listed_price),2) list_bill,
       ROUND(SUM(seat_count*(listed_price-effective_price)),2) promo_gap
FROM bills GROUP BY bill_day, days_ahead ORDER BY bill_day
"""))
show('billing schedule by week next 12 weeks', q(f"""
WITH RECURSIVE offs(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM offs WHERE x<84),
bills AS (
 SELECT ((x-1)/7)+1 AS wk, {DAY}+x AS bill_day, s.subscription_id, c.group_id, s.plan, s.seat_count, s.effective_price, s.listed_price
 FROM offs JOIN subscriptions s ON s.status='subscribed' AND (({DAY}+x) % 30)=s.billing_day_mod30
 JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
)
SELECT wk, MIN(bill_day) start_day, MAX(bill_day) end_day, COUNT(*) subs, ROUND(SUM(seat_count*effective_price),2) eff_bill, ROUND(SUM(seat_count*listed_price),2) list_bill
FROM bills GROUP BY wk ORDER BY wk
"""))
show('billing schedule by group/plan next 30', q(f"""
WITH RECURSIVE offs(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM offs WHERE x<30)
SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) bills, ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.effective_price),2) eff_bill, ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*s.listed_price),2) list_bill,
       ROUND(SUM(s.seat_count*(s.listed_price-s.effective_price)),2) promo_gap
FROM offs JOIN subscriptions s ON s.status='subscribed' AND (({DAY}+x)%30)=s.billing_day_mod30
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan ORDER BY eff_bill DESC
"""))
# usage
show('service last 21 days', q(f"""

FROM service_day WHERE day>{DAY}-21 ORDER BY day
"""))
show('usage last 7 by active group/plan', q(f"""

       COUNT(u.customer_id) usage_rows, SUM(u.usage_units) units,

FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
LEFT JOIN daily_usage u ON u.customer_id=s.customer_id AND u.day>{DAY}-7 AND u.day<={DAY}
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan ORDER BY units DESC
"""))
show('usage last 7 by group plan listed', q(f"""

       SUM(u.usage_units) units, ROUND(1.0*SUM(u.usage_units)/COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id)/7,1) units_per_user_day,
       ROUND(SUM(u.usage_units)*CASE s.plan WHEN 'C' THEN 0.006 ELSE 0.002 END,2) compute_week,
       ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id)*s.effective_price,2) mrr
FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
LEFT JOIN daily_usage u ON u.customer_id=s.customer_id AND u.day>{DAY}-7 AND u.day<={DAY}
WHERE s.status='subscribed'
GROUP BY c.group_id, s.plan, ROUND(s.listed_price,2), ROUND(s.effective_price,2)
ORDER BY c.group_id, s.plan, units DESC
"""))
show('usage distribution active by group plan', q(f"""
WITH u AS (
 SELECT s.customer_id, c.group_id, s.plan, SUM(CASE WHEN du.day>{DAY}-7 AND du.day<={DAY} THEN du.usage_units ELSE 0 END)/7.0 AS avg_daily
 FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id
 LEFT JOIN daily_usage du ON du.customer_id=s.customer_id AND du.day>{DAY}-7 AND du.day<={DAY}
